name: Fix a pod wired to a missing RuntimeClass
objective: CKS › Minimize Microservice Vulnerabilities. Drill EVERY RuntimeClass corner harder than the exam: create a class and its required handler, the optional scheduling/overhead fields, select it per-pod and per-Deployment, contrast with the default runtime, layer securityContext hardening on top, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a pod wired to a RuntimeClass that doesn't exist
questions.teach:
A pod naming a `runtimeClassName` the cluster doesn't have is rejected with **RuntimeClass … not found** and never schedules. `kubectl describe pod

` shows the bad name. Fix it to an existing class. **Gotcha:** `runtimeClassName` is **immutable** on an existing pod — you must delete and recreate the pod with the correct class name; editing it in place is rejected.
questions.prompt:
Pod `brokenrc` in `runtimeclass-learn` won't schedule — its `runtimeClassName` names a class that doesn't exist. Diagnose the fault and fix it so the pod references a VALID existing RuntimeClass (`gvisor`). Keep image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`.

Target: pod `brokenrc` exists with `.spec.runtimeClassName` = `gvisor` (a class that actually exists). (As in step 3, the runsc handler is absent so the pod stays Pending — we grade the corrected spec, not the phase.)
questions.hint: `kubectl -n runtimeclass-learn describe pod brokenrc` → runtimeClassName is a typo (`gvisro`). runtimeClassName is immutable, so `kubectl delete pod brokenrc` and recreate it with `runtimeClassName: gvisor`.
questions.solution:
# describe shows runtimeClassName 'gvisro' (typo) — the class doesn't exist.
kubectl -n runtimeclass-learn delete pod brokenrc --ignore-not-found
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: brokenrc, namespace: runtimeclass-learn }
spec:
  runtimeClassName: gvisor
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
YAML

verification.description: 'brokenrc' is Running with a valid runtimeClassName gvisor (typo fixed)

questions.eli5:
A pod can ask for a runtime by name — but if it names one the cluster has never heard of, Kubernetes won't guess or fall back. It just says **"RuntimeClass … not found"** and the pod never schedules. It's like ordering "the Deluxe plan" at a shop that only sells "Standard" and "Premium" — the cashier can't ring it up, so nothing happens.

Here, pod `brokenrc` asks for a class that doesn't exist (a typo — `gvisro` instead of `gvisor`). Your job is detective + repair:

1. **Diagnose:** `kubectl describe pod brokenrc` shows the bad `runtimeClassName` and the "not found" complaint in the events.
2. **Fix:** point it at a class that actually exists — `gvisor`.

The sting in the tail: `runtimeClassName` is **immutable**. You can't just edit the running pod to fix the typo — Kubernetes refuses. You have to **delete the pod and recreate it** with the correct name. (Same as before: with no `runsc` installed it'll stay Pending, but the grader only checks that the corrected spec names `gvisor`.)

**Watch out for:**

- A pod naming a non-existent `runtimeClassName` is **rejected / never schedules** — error "RuntimeClass … not found"; no silent fallback to default.
- `runtimeClassName` is **immutable** — you **cannot edit it in place**; `kubectl edit` is rejected. Delete and recreate.
- **Diagnose with `kubectl describe pod brokenrc`** — the events/spec reveal the typo'd class name.
- Fix to an **existing** class (`gvisor`), not another typo — double-check against `kubectl get runtimeclass`.
- The pod may stay **Pending** (missing `runsc` handler) — that's expected; the corrected spec is what's graded.
questions.deepDive:
## Fixing a pod wired to a missing RuntimeClass — full rundown

### Mental model
`runtimeClassName` must resolve to an **existing** RuntimeClass at admission. If it doesn't, the pod is **rejected / stuck** with `RuntimeClass "<name>" not found` — there is **no fallback** to the default runtime. Because the field is **immutable**, the fix is always: diagnose the bad name, then **delete and recreate** the pod with a valid class. This is the standard troubleshooting loop: `describe → identify → delete → recreate → verify`.

### The failure modes (know the difference)
| Cause | Where it fails | Message |
|---|---|---|
| `runtimeClassName` names a **non-existent** class (typo `gvisro`) | admission | `RuntimeClass "gvisro" not found` → pod never schedules |
| class exists but **handler missing on node** | kubelet / node | `Pending` / `RunContainerError` (handler not found) |
| class exists + handler present | runs | sandboxed |

This lab is the **first** case: a typo'd class name.

### Step 1 — diagnose
```bash
kubectl -n runtimeclass-learn describe pod brokenrc
# Status: Pending; Events: "RuntimeClass \"gvisro\" not found"
kubectl -n runtimeclass-learn get pod brokenrc -o jsonpath='{.spec.runtimeClassName}'; echo   # gvisro
kubectl get runtimeclass        # confirm the real name is 'gvisor'
```

### Step 2 — fix (delete + recreate, because it's immutable)
`runtimeClassName` is **immutable**; `kubectl edit`/`patch` on it is rejected (`field is immutable`). Recreate:
```bash
kubectl -n runtimeclass-learn delete pod brokenrc --ignore-not-found
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: brokenrc, namespace: runtimeclass-learn }
spec:
  runtimeClassName: gvisor        # corrected to an existing class
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
YAML
```

### Step 3 — verify
```bash
kubectl -n runtimeclass-learn get pod brokenrc -o jsonpath='{.spec.runtimeClassName}'; echo   # gvisor
```
With `runsc` absent the pod stays **Pending** (handler not installed) — **the corrected `.spec.runtimeClassName == gvisor` is the graded signal**, not the phase.

### Why no fallback
RuntimeClass admission is strict by design: silently downgrading a workload that asked for a sandbox to the shared-kernel default would be a **security regression**. So Kubernetes fails closed — better a Pending pod than an unexpectedly unsandboxed one.

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **No silent fallback** — a bad class name blocks scheduling with `RuntimeClass … not found`; it does not quietly run on `runc`.
- **`runtimeClassName` is immutable** — never `kubectl edit`; always delete + recreate.
- **Diagnose via `describe`** — the events name the exact (typo'd) class.
- Fix to a **real** class (`gvisor`); verify the spelling against `kubectl get runtimeclass`.
- Distinguish **class-not-found** (admission) from **handler-not-found** (node) — both yield Pending but have different causes; here it's the former.
- Pending due to missing `runsc` after the fix is expected; grade is the spec.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl -n runtimeclass-learn describe pod brokenrc       # see 'gvisro' not found
kubectl -n runtimeclass-learn delete pod brokenrc
# recreate with runtimeClassName: gvisor
kubectl -n runtimeclass-learn get pod brokenrc -o jsonpath='{.spec.runtimeClassName}'; echo   # gvisor
```
